caption:
OpenAI hired former US Army Secretary Dan Driscoll for a brand new national security role.
He will advise OpenAI's leaders and partners on how AI can strengthen national and cyber security, working with US allies.
Driscoll resigned in August after months of tension with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.

Should AI companies be hiring Pentagon leaders?

paragraphs.text: OpenAI announced on November 2, 2026 that it has appointed Dan Driscoll, a former US Secretary of the Army, to a newly created position: Senior Counselor for National Security Modernization. According to Reuters, he will advise the company's leadership and work with outside partners on how advanced AI can strengthen national security and cybersecurity.

OpenAI said Driscoll will engage government officials, industry leaders and academic institutions on practical initiatives for what the company calls democratic AI. Reuters reported that he will also help OpenAI's internal teams understand the operational needs of national security organizations around the world.

Unite.AI, summarizing the announcement, listed further duties: advising public and private partners on policy and strategy changes that could bring practical AI uses to national security, and identifying where operational needs, institutional change and new AI capabilities meet. Gizmodo reported that the role puts particular weight on working with US allies on responsible use.

In a statement quoted by Reuters, Driscoll said: "I'm joining OpenAI to help the United States and our allies put this technology to work responsibly." He also said AI could help militaries keep pace by cutting through paperwork and making sense of more information, according to Gizmodo. OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman said the appointment would help the United States and described it as an opportunity to work with other countries to spread the adoption of democratic AI.
Driscoll's path from the Army to OpenAI

Driscoll served as the 26th Secretary of the Army, overseeing resources for nearly one million active, Guard and Reserve soldiers and more than 265,000 Army civilians, according to Unite.AI. He also served as acting director of the ATF. Reuters noted that President Trump picked him to take part in talks with Moscow and Kyiv aimed at ending the war in Ukraine, an unusual diplomatic assignment for an Army secretary.

He resigned in August after months of tension with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, Reuters and Gizmodo reported. Gizmodo, citing an anonymously sourced Politico report, said the disagreements centered on initiatives to modernize the Army, and that the firing of popular Pentagon figures, including Army Chief of Staff Randy George, also played a part.

Before the Pentagon, Driscoll worked at BlackArch Partners, an investment bank in Charlotte, North Carolina, Gizmodo reported. He served in Iraq in 2009 and received the Army Commendation Medal and the Combat Action Badge. Gizmodo also described him as a longtime friend of Vice President J.D. Vance from their time at Yale Law School.

In NeuraFeed's reading, the hire signals that OpenAI wants a direct line into how defense ministries and their allies buy and deploy technology. A former service secretary who led a push to field new tools faster brings both credibility and connections, and the focus on allies fits OpenAI's broader pitch of spreading US built AI abroad. The political baggage of a public split with the current Pentagon leadership may also shape how the role is received in Washington.

The next signal to watch is which governments and allied institutions OpenAI announces as partners in this national security work, and whether any of the projects Driscoll advises on move into formal contracts.
